findings.scope: Envelope refusal precedence and closed error vocabulary
findings.title: Canonical-profile envelope mutations take the wrong RJ-4 refusal class
findings.probe: Starting with the retained valid manifest envelope and admitted root, change only envelopeSchema from integer 2 to float 2.0 (also reproduced with an NFD string mutation). verify_envelope returns ('RJ-4 ENVELOPE_MISMATCH', 'boundary exception Reject').
findings.expected: Section 2.2 step 1 owns malformed envelope presence/structure and maps it to RJ-4 UNSIGNED, as the unknown-member and missing-member controls do. Canonical profile rejection occurs before routing, digest or signature use and must use that same malformed-envelope class.
findings.impact: The boundary fails closed and no signature verifies, so this is not a security-authority bypass. It is an exact contract/refusal-precedence mismatch consumed by the closed protocol vocabulary; the outer fallback also exposes an exception class in its detail.
findings.requiredRepair: Catch the canonical-profile Reject alongside SchemaError in step 1 and return the fixed malformed-envelope refusal ('RJ-4 UNSIGNED', 'malformed envelope: canonical profile'); retain integer success, float/NFD refusal, routing mismatch precedence and the fixed outer fallback token.
